rows.citation: Onasch S, Gjorgjieva J (2020). Circuit Stability to Perturbations Reveals Hidden Variability in the Balance of Intrinsic and Synaptic Conductances. The Journal of Neuroscience, 40(16), 3186-3202.
rows.model_type: Degenerate population of conductance-based two-neuron half-center oscillator circuits (stomatogastric-type channel kinetics)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial: systematic single and double maximal-conductance perturbations (down to deletion, up to 200%), but as biological perturbations, not recorded model-edit faults
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: perturbations are parameter changes to spontaneously rhythmic circuits; no battery of current-clamp stimulation protocols
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial: rhythmic circuit output (e.g. bursting pattern) summarised into a global stability measure; not an eFEL-style single-cell feature set
rows.protocol_optimization: no: clusters conductances by perturbation response; does not select a compact test set
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: no discovery/held-out split of models or perturbation families for a detection method
rows.ai_transformations: no: no AI-assisted or software transformations
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Conceptual support that similar-looking models diverge under perturbation. NeuroSem instead tests edited NeuroML files with stimulus batteries, calibrated tolerances, mutants and held-out selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API work record (title, authors, volume/issue/pages, dates); Europe PMC REST abstract; NCBI E-utilities PMC full text (methods, code availability statement)
rows.found_via: WebSearch degenerate conductance-based models perturbation query; Crossref; abstract via Europe PMC

rows.citation: Tomko M, Lupascu CA, Filipova A, et al. (2026). Functionally convergent but parametrically distinct solutions: Robust degeneracy in a population of computational models of early-birth rat CA1 pyramidal neurons. bioRxiv (preprint).
rows.model_type: Populations of biophysically detailed multicompartment CA1 pyramidal neuron models (NEURON/BluePyOpt), 10 morphologies
rows.controlled_mutations: no: generates many parameter sets by optimisation; no deliberate single-fault mutants of a reference model
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: short depolarising pulses, prolonged depolarising steps and hyperpolarising steps at several amplitudes
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: 182 somatic e-features extracted with BluePyEfe constrain the optimisation
rows.protocol_optimization: no: optimises model parameters (CMA-ES), not the choice of stimulation protocols
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial: features at current amplitudes excluded from optimisation used for post-hoc generalisation, plus cross-morphology tests; not held-out fault detection
rows.software: none released yet (preprint states code will be archived on Zenodo/GitHub upon acceptance); uses BluePyOpt, BluePyEModel, BluePyEfe
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows feature-matched models can hide parametric differences, and uses held-out amplitudes for generalisation. NeuroSem targets detection of edits/mutants with optimised protocol batteries.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API work record; bioRxiv details API (authors, date, licence); bioRxiv JATS source XML (methods, stimuli, generalisation, data availability); Europe PMC REST search confirms PPR1217004
rows.found_via: Europe PMC refined features/generalization query; abstract via Europe PMC

rows.model_type: Experimental patch-clamp recordings and reconstructions of mouse visual cortex neurons (1,938 cells); unsupervised classification
rows.controlled_mutations: no: recorded cells; no controlled model faults
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: standardised current-clamp protocol with square pulses, ramps and noisy current injections
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: many e-features from membrane potential and action potential waveforms, reduced by sparse PCA
rows.protocol_optimization: no: stimulus set fixed; analysis selects components for clustering, not stimuli
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: unsupervised taxonomy; no held-out fault-detection evaluation
rows.software: IPFX https://github.com/alleninstitute/ipfx ; drcme https://github.com/alleninstitute/drcme ; AllenSDK (links cited in paper)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows multi-stimulus features discriminate neuron types. NeuroSem applies such features to detect behavioural change between a reference model and edited variants.

rows.model_type: General software engineering: graph-based system models (directed graphs, event sequence graphs, FSMs, statecharts) of industrial systems
rows.controlled_mutations: yes: elementary insertion and omission mutation operators applied to models to create mutants
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: test cases (event sequences) generated from mutated models; no electrical stimulation

rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic model-level mutation testing background. NeuroSem mutates biophysical NeuroML models and measures continuous electrophysiology features against calibrated tolerances.
